messages.author: 611cd8917db7dbfa
messages.subject: data for covarying analysis
parts:
Hi,
I am interested in using Coll.analysis 3.2a to do covarying analysis
for Korean multi-verb construction (e.g., "V1-conjuction V2").

It seems that only text file with raw data like example 1 can be used
for covarying analysis.

Example1
word1 word2
word1 word2
word1 word2
word1 word3
word1 word3
word2 word4

However, I only have a tabulated list of all cooccurrences like
example 2

Example 2
slot1 slot2 frequency
word1 word2 3
word1 word3 2
word2 word4 1

Is there any way to use the second type of input file (i.e. Example2)
to the Coll.analysis3.2a for covarying anslysis? Or should I convert
all the data into the type like example1. Do anyone know how to do it
automatically?
Thanks,

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] data for covarying analysis
parts:
Hi

That is a very good question. In fact, an older version of the script
accepted both types of input, the raw data that are still accepted AND
the tabulated version you have right now. However, at one point of
time I discontinued supporting the second kind of input so, yes, you
will have to convert the data to the usual case-by-variable format.
You can do this like this:

data.new <- as.data.frame(lapply(data.old[,1:2], function (x) rep(x,
data.all[,dim(data.all)[2]]))) # code from Michael J. Crawley
(2007:189)


Cheers,
STG

messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Re: data for covarying analysis
parts:
Uh, the reference was included: Crawley's "The R book". You need to
load the cross-tabulated data frame into R as data.old, then run this
line (there was a typo in the previous version),
data.new <- as.data.frame(lapply(data.old[,1:2], function (x) rep(x,

data.old[,dim(data.old)[2]]))) # code from Michael J. Crawley
(2007:189)

and then save that result as a tab-delimited text file. If you don't
know what all that means, then you have to do it some other way,
probably with your spreadsheet software.

messages.author: 5230e5cecde250f0
messages.subject: Re: data for covarying analysis
parts:
Yong, here is a less elegant, but (I think) more transparent solution
for learning-about-R purposes:

words.1<-as.character(data.old[,1])
words.2<-as.character(data.old[,2])
strings.1<-paste(words.1, words.2)
strings.2<-rep(strings.1, data.old[,3])
strings.3<-strsplit(strings.2, " ")
strings.4<-sapply(strings.3, "[")
strings.5<-t(strings.4)
data.new<-as.data.frame(strings.5)

These steps could be nested into one line of code, but at the cost of
the transparency:

data.new<-
as.data.frame(t(sapply(strsplit(rep(paste(as.character(data.old[,1]),
as.character(data.old[,2])), data.old[,3]), " "), "[")))

Best. Earl Brown
